title: Dynamical control of particle jets from a driven condensate in a one-dimensional lattice with double-well potential
abstract: We investigate the nonlinear dynamics of a Bose-Einstein condensate trapped in a double-well potential of a one-dimensional lattice, where the interatomic interactions are periodically modulated in time. In the typical case of a symmetric double-well, we observe collective particle emission under resonant driving, where the excitation regimes are explicitly constrained by the interplay between the drive strength and the hopping amplitude. By introducing a depth asymmetry between the wells, we find that moderate bias specifically enhances the emission rate, while large asymmetry suppresses it. The particle jets can be further controlled by modulating the hopping amplitudes, where the emission is weakened for finite hopping imbalances. These results outline the roles of asymmetry and external driving in precisely manipulating quantum many-body transport, and may offer insights into the design of atomtronic devices.
summary: This paper theoretically explores how external driving and structural asymmetries can be used to control the emission of particles from a Bose-Einstein condensate confined in a double-well lattice. By tuning parameters like well depth bias or hopping imbalance, researchers demonstrated methods to enhance or suppress quantum particle jets, offering insights for building atomtronic devices.
main_problem: The study investigates the nonlinear dynamics of particle jets emitted from a Bose-Einstein condensate trapped in a double-well potential subjected to time-periodic external driving.
main_result: The emission rate can be precisely controlled by tuning the depth asymmetry between the wells or by modulating the hopping amplitudes, demonstrating tunable quantum many-body transport.
method: The analysis uses mean-field approximations and solves coupled differential equations derived from a Hamiltonian describing the driven condensate dynamics in the double well.
model_or_system: The system is a Bose-Einstein condensate confined to a one-dimensional lattice with a double-well potential, where interatomic interactions are periodically modulated. The model incorporates hopping terms, on-site potentials, and time-dependent driving fields.
key_observables: Particle emission rate ($\xi$), total particle number decay ($N_0(t)$), and particle imbalance between the two wells.
important_parameters: Drive strength ($g$), lattice hopping amplitude ($J$), depth asymmetry ($\Delta V = V_b - V_c$), and hopping imbalance ($\Delta J = J_b - J_c$).
main_assumptions: The analysis often proceeds using the mean-field approximation, sometimes simplifying to $U=0$ or employing a two-mode approximation ansatz.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate excitation regimes based on drive strength and hopping amplitude (Fig. 2), particle number decay over time under varying driving frequencies (Fig. 3), and dependence of emission rate on depth asymmetry ($\Delta V$) and hopping imbalance ($\Delta J$).
paper_structure:

why_interesting: This work directly addresses controllable quantum transport phenomena using ultracold atoms (BECs) in engineered potentials, which is a major focus area for AMO physics and atomtronic device design.
